annotations.title: Share a piece of your own with others

description: Share a piece of the working folder with everybody who uses Cutscene. It is first passed through the gates here (check_piece: a piece that fails is not sent), then kept on the user's account and sent to the person of the Cutscene team who checks what is shared; nothing is visible to others before that person accepts it (their answer comes within 3 days at most), and the user can take it back from their account page (« Mes partages »). A template may start from another one, not copy it: one whose cut is more than two thirds the same as a template already in the library is refused, and the refusal names that template. What leaves is the piece alone (its recipe, with its example words): never a film, its words, its logo or its pictures. It needs the app's address and a key of the user's account (CUTSCENE_APP_URL, CUTSCENE_TOKEN), confirm: true, and the user's word first: their piece leaves their machine, under the name they choose to show (public_name) or none. Sharing is a permission its author gives, each time: before confirm: true, put it to the user in their own language and get their yes. The permission: “By sharing, you allow Cutscene, free of charge, to show this piece in its library, and its users to use it and change it in their films, commercial and advertising ones included, without having to credit you (Terms, article 12). If you remove the share, the films already made with it keep it. Sharing is for adults only.” Sharing the same piece again sends a new version, and needs their yes again.

confirm.description: Must be true: say so only once the user read the permission and agreed to share this piece

id.description: The id of a piece of the working folder (see search_library { mine: true })

public_name.description: The name shown next to the piece as its author. Left out: the one the account already shows, or none
